AARON A. CAPAO, JR. Sangguniang Bayan Member Chairman, Committee on Rules Municipality of San Francisco Province of Cebu Dear Hon. Capao, Jr.: 46 s. zog_ This has reference to your letter dated 4 May 2018 requesting the Department's opinion/clarification on the legality of some provisions of your proposed ordinance, re: 'IANORDINANCEESTABLISHING FIRE HYDRANTS AND TER SUPPL YFOR FIRE PROTECTION WITHIN THEMUNICIPALITYOFSAIVFRAIVCISCO, CEBU'; to wit: 1. Any water service providers whether private, cooperative or local government units shall be required to establish/install fire hydrants in their respective serviced areas. 2. Public fire hydrants shall be spaced a maximum of 350 feet apart. 3. When any portion of the building protected is in excess of 350 feet from a public fire hydrant, there shall be provided by the building owner, onsite fire hydrant and mains capable of supplying the required fire flow. 4. Private fire hydrants for single family residences equipped with fire sprinklers shall have fire hydrants spaced a maximum of 500 feet apart. 5. The LGU shall take-over the operation and management of the water service to those water service providers who violates the ordinance. In addition, you also posed the following queries, viz: 6. Is there any limitation provided by law with regard to the imposition of excessive fees and charges imposed by LGUs particularly the barangays? This is because there is a certain barangay in their municipality imposing P5,OOO.00 barangay clearance fee to resorts, gasoline stations and other bigger businesses.

7. What is the appropriate distance from institutions provided by law for the establishment of lotto outlets and/or STLs? At the outset, in the review of an ordinance, the basic rule is that the subject of the ordinance must not be violative of any national laws and the passage or amendment thereof must be within the corporate powers of the city to enact and must be in accordance with the procedure prescribed by law, the Local Government Code (LGCY. Fer aes. 2. and 4 To enlighten you on the matter, allow us to present the provisions of the national law which we find pertinent to your queries, to wit: l. Section 13-C of Republic Act (RA) NO. 9514, otherwise known as the "Fire Code of the Philippines of 2008"provides that: "SECTION 13-C. Use of Income Generated from the Enforcement of the Fire Code. — The Chief, BFP is authorized, subject to the approval of the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government, to use the income generated under the Fire Code for procurement of fire protection and fire fighting investigation, rescue, paramedics, supplies and materials, and related technical services necessary for the fire service and the improvement of facilites of the Bureau of Fire Protection and abatement of fire hazards. The BFP shall determine the number Of equipment. ve I v rn h c an ni o he ro r elive fi protection in fts jurisdiction. In the procurement of fire fighting and investigation supplies and materials, the Bureau of Product Standards of' the Department of Trade and Industry shall evaluate, determine and certifyifthe supply to procured conforms to theproduct standards fixed by the BFP. For this purpose, the BFP shall submit to the Bureau of Product Standards a detailed set of product standards that must be complied with in the procurement of fire fighting and investigation supplies and materials within six (6) months from the effectivity of this act. " (Underscoring supplied) 2. Section 10.5.7.1(B) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA NO. 9514 states that: " DILG Legal Opinion no. 34, S.2018 dated 25

3. 4. "Local Government Units (LGUs) in coordination with the BFPsha11 provide each community with fire hydrants and cisterns or elevated tanks that will suffice the requirement pertaining to provision of water for fire fighting operation. " Section 48 of Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1982 or the "Provincial Water Utilities Act of 1973'; viz: 'Section 48. Charter. - There is hereby chartered, created and formed a national agency to be known as the "Local Water Utilities Administration " which is hereby attached to the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA). The provisions Of this Title shall be and constitute the charter of the Administration. Section 49 of PD No. 198, to wit: 'Section 49. Purposes. - The purposes for which the Administration is created are: (1) to establish minimum standards and regulations in order to assure acceptable standards of construction materials and supplies, maintenance, operation, personnel, training, accounting and fiscal practices for local water utilities; (2) to furnish technical assistance and personnel training programs for local water utilities; (3) to monitor and evaluate local water standards; (4) to effect system integration, joint investment and operations district annexation and deannexation whenever economically warranted; and (5) to provide a specialized lending institution with peculiar expertise in the financing of local water utilities. " It is clear from the foregoing provisions of law that the concerned LGU shall coordinate with the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) concerning the establishments Of fire hydrants as they are vested with authority to determine the optimal number of fire hydrants required by every local government unit for the proper delivery of fire protection services in their respective jurisdiction. As to the proposed provision that the LGU shall take-over the operation and management of the water service to those water service providers who violates the ordinance, this Department is of the considered view that the same is violative Of PD NO. 198 as again, it is the Local Utilities Administration (LWUA) that has the power and duty to establish minimum standards and regulations for local water utilities, and adopt rules and regulations for the enforcement thereof3. Said standards and regulations under Section 62 thereof includes the following, to wit: 25 May 1973 Section 62, PDN0. 198

XXX AX.V "(c) Equipment, Materials and Supplies. Standards for the optimum selection and effective utilization of equipment, materials and supplies by local water and sewer utilities; (d) Operations and Maintenance. Standardized procedures for operating and maintaining equipment and facilities. " xxx xxx As to the imposition of barangay clearance fee, Section 1524 of the Local Government Code (LGC) has given the sanggunian barangay wide latitude to impose reasonable fees. The reasonableness of a fee would depend on the regulatory service to be rendered by the barangay in relation to the issuance of a barangay clearance. Fees and charges should be proportionate or equal to the cost Of issuing the license or permit and the expenses incurred6. Hence, the determination of whether the imposition of barangay clearance fee is excessive will depend on the cost of issuing the license or permit and the expenses incurred. F r u no. Scope of Taxing Powers. - The barangays may levy taxes, fees, and charges, as provided in this Article, which shall exclusively accrue to them: (c) Barangay Clearance. - No city or municipality may issue any license or permit for any business or activity unless a clearance is first obtained from the barangay where such business or activity is located or conducted. For such clearance, the sangguniang barangay The application for clearance Shal/ be acted upon within seven (7) working days from the filing thereof. C. Churches — 100 meters Be that as it may, we recommend that the inputs and comments of the PCSO be solicited as the subject matter hereof pertains to their competency. Hence, this Department's position on the appropriate distance from institutions to lotto outlets and/or STLs shall be without prejudice to the position of the PCSO.
